title: Braden Kelley — 'Is it Possible to be Incorruptible?' Exclusive Interview with Eric Ries
summary: Braden Kelley — LinkedIn Top Voice, keynote speaker, and futurist behind a 17,000+ subscriber innovation newsletter — publishes an 11-question exclusive Q&A with Eric on Incorruptible, covering the physics of organizations, financial gravity vs magnetic alignment, constitutional governance vs super-voting shares, why mission primacy is the successor to shareholder primacy, and why two-entity structures (Novo Nordisk / Patagonia / Tony's Chocolonely) are the most stable corporate form.
blockquote: I believe that the era of shareholder primacy is actually already over, for two reasons. One is, this is an idea that has proved to be self-defeating. It was originally enacted — not in ancient times, but in the 1980s, at least in Delaware — to be beneficial to shareholders, but that is not how it has proved.
blockquote_source: Eric Ries, quoted in Braden Kelley interview
